Verdict: faithful (not refuted). After a clause-by-clause comparison I found no place where the Lean type is weaker than the printed thm:A-soft; every difference makes the Lean statement stronger, and the printed statement is a literal instance of it.

(a) Hypotheses. Source: "Let P be generic, q admissible, and ε₀ as in Lemma lem:soft-generic." Lean: `hP : Generic P` (= G1 ∧ G2, matching def:generic (G1)/(G2) verbatim: `G1 P := ∀ i j k, i≠j → j≠k → i≠k → chi P i j k ≠ 0`, `G2` = no point in three distinct `edgeInterior`s); `hq : SoftAdmissible P j q := det (edge P (j-1)) q ≠ 0 ∧ det q (edge P j) ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ k ≠ j, det q (P k - P j) ≠ 0`, exactly def:soft's three conditions "det(λ_{j-1},q)≠0, det(q,λ_j)≠0, det(q,μ_k−μ_j)≠0 for all k≠j" (q≠0 follows; `SoftAdmissible.vector_ne_zero`); `hn : 3 ≤ n` is def:polygon's n ≥ 3. ε₀: the Lean takes an arbitrary `(ε0 : ℝ) (hε0 : 0 < ε0)` and returns `ε1` with `0 < ε1 ∧ ε1 ≤ ε0`. Since the Lean is universally quantified over ε0, instantiating ε0 := the ε₀ of lem:soft-generic gives the printed "there is ε₁ ∈ (0, ε₀]". This covers the printed statement in either reading (ε₀ a specific witness of the lemma, or any positive number for which the lemma's conclusions hold); the Lean is strictly stronger (it holds for every positive ε0), never weaker.

(b) Quantifiers. Source: "For every root g of P_ε other than the soft edge ... there is ε₁ ∈ (0,ε₀] with (identity) (0<ε<ε₁)" — ∀ root ∃ ε₁, so ε₁ may depend on the root. Lean: `∃ ε1, 0 < ε1 ∧ ε1 ≤ ε0 ∧ ∀ ε, 0 < ε → ε < ε1 → ∃ hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε), ∀ a, a ≠ softOldIndex j j → ...` — one ε1 for all roots. ∃ε1∀a implies ∀a∃ε₁ (take the same ε1 for every root), so the Lean is stronger. The extra conclusion `Generic (softInsertion P j q ε)` (the source gets it from lem:soft-generic (i), and needs it to make A_g(P_ε) meaningful) is again a strengthening, not a hypothesis.

(c) Root correspondence. Source: roots are edge indices (def:root: "an edge index g ∈ Z/n, the root edge being E_g from μ_g to μ_{g+1}"); P_ε = (μ_1,…,μ_j, μ_j+εq, μ_{j+1},…,μ_n), soft edge εq, return edge λ_j−εq, "the others unchanged"; correspondence: "Identify each unchanged edge with its parent edge and the return edge with the parent edge E_j" (lem:soft-generic (iii); thm: "the return edge corresponds to E_j"). Lean: `softInsertion P j q ε a = Fin.insertNth (softNewPosition j) (P j + ε • q) (fun k => P (boundaryIndex 0 k)) (canonicalPosition a)` with `softNewPosition j = canonicalPosition j + 1`, i.e. μ_* inserted at label label(j)+1 with labels ≤ label(j) kept and later labels shifted by one (`softOldIndex_physical`, `softNewIndex_physical`) — exactly the printed tuple, including j = n (μ_* at label n+1 ≡ 0). `softInsertion_old/new`, `edge_softInsertion_soft : edge (P_ε) (softOldIndex j j) = ε • q`, `edge_softInsertion_return : edge (P_ε) (softNewIndex j) = edge P j - ε • q`, `edge_softInsertion_old (k≠j) : edge (P_ε) (softOldIndex j k) = edge P k`. So the soft edge is root `softOldIndex j j` (excluded by `a ≠ softOldIndex j j`), and `softParentEdge j k := if k = j then softNewIndex j else softOldIndex j k` sends E_j to the return edge and every other E_k to the unchanged copy of E_k (its start vertex μ_k has label `softOldIndex j k`, and `softOldIndex_next : softOldIndex j (k+1) = softOldIndex j k + 1` for k≠j, `softNewIndex_next : softNewIndex j + 1 = softOldIndex j (j+1)`). `softParentEdge_injective`, `softParentEdge_ne_soft`, `soft_parent_edges_exhaust` make it a bijection roots(P) → roots(P_ε)∖{soft edge}. The Lean `∃! g, a = softParentEdge j g ∧ Φ g` therefore asserts Φ at exactly the corresponding root g' of the source (uniqueness is automatic from injectivity; existence carries the content). Not weaker.

(d) Identity and multiplier. Source: A_g(P_ε) = ((χ_−+χ_+)/2) A_{g'}(P), with χ_− = −sgn det(λ_{j−1},q), χ_+ = −sgn det(q,λ_j) (def:soft). Lean: `softAttachmentMinus P j q := -SignType.sign (det (edge P (j - 1)) q)`, `softAttachmentPlus P j q := -SignType.sign (det q (edge P j))` (edge P i = P(i+1) − P i = λ_i) — same signs, same argument order; `softAmplitudeMultiplier P j q : ℚ := (((χ_- : ℤ) : ℚ) + ((χ_+ : ℤ) : ℚ)) / 2` — exact rational average, no integer division; the identity `(treeCoefficient P_ε hQ.1 a _ : ℚ) = softAmplitudeMultiplier P j q * (treeCoefficient P hP.1 g hn : ℚ)` is the printed identity with both integers cast to ℚ (ℤ→ℚ injective, so equivalent to the integer statement). Sectors: the only definitions of the sector names in the source are lem:soft-generic (iv) lines 1040–1043: same-sign χ_−=χ_+=−τ, mixed χ_−≠χ_+, loop χ_−=χ_+=τ, with τ = τ_j(P); the thm says the multipliers are −τ_j(P), 0, τ_j(P) respectively. Lean: `(softAttachmentMinus = -turn P j ∧ softAttachmentPlus = -turn P j) → A_a(P_ε) = -(turn P j : ℤ) * A_g(P)`; `(softAttachmentMinus ≠ softAttachmentPlus) → A_a(P_ε) = 0`; `(softAttachmentMinus = turn P j ∧ softAttachmentPlus = turn P j) → A_a(P_ε) = (turn P j : ℤ) * A_g(P)`, with `turn P i := chi P (i-1) i (i+1)` = τ_i = χ_{i−1,i,i+1} (def:chirotope). Signs and sector conditions are exactly the printed ones; stating them as integer conjuncts in addition to the ℚ identity is a (consistent) strengthening.

(e) Primitives. `treeCoefficient P hP g hn := rootedTreeRec ordinary rootWeight (fullBoundaryInterval hn)` = Σ over all compositions π of [0, n−1] (one-part included) of `rootWeight π * ∏ openTreeRec (part k)`; `openTreeRec I = if I.leaves = 1 then 1 else -Σ_{π, 2 ≤ parts} ordinary π * ∏ openTreeRec (part k)`; `ordinaryWeight/rootWeight = ∏_{interior cuts} ordinaryGate/rootGate (nearSign) (farSign)` with `ordinaryGate d h = d * Θ(−h d)`, `rootGate d h = d * Θ(h d)`, `signTheta s = if s = 1 then 1 else 0`; `nearSign k = chi P a_{r_{k+1}} a_{r_k} a_{r_{k−1}}`, `farSign k = chi P a_j a_{r_k} a_i` via `boundaryIndex g k = g + k + 1` (a_k = μ_{g+1+k}, a_{n−1} = μ_g); `chi P i j k = sign (det (P j - P i) (P k - P i))`. This is def:root/def:gates/def:treesum verbatim (V^+, V^−, b_{[i,i+1]}=1, b_{[i,j]} recursion with |π|≥2, A_g over all compositions of [0,N]). For P_ε the same definition is applied on ZMod (n+1) with `3 ≤ n+1`.
